stage1.impression: It looks like a CG showroom seen through a shop window, not a photograph of a particular shop. The Ember pair glows like neon signage. The back half of the room drops to near black, the shelves are almost empty and nobody is in it. A hard-edged blue rectangle (a reflection or a compositing artefact) cuts across the middle of the frame, and the brightest, sharpest thing in the picture is a regular CG paving pattern in the foreground. A design magazine would not run this as a specific place. It reads as a generic, unpeopled shop render.

blocking_9: The Tropos pair is the clear hero: speaker region lum_median >= 45 with the batts and the cast edges legible, not a flat red glow
No hard-edged blue reflection rectangle across the interior; the glass reflects only a dim, warm, believable street
The back of the shop (felt, bar, listening room) holds detail: crush_pct < 25 and frame lum_median between 22 and 50
The shelves are stocked like a working shop (records face-out, product, cards), with signs of life (glasses on the bar, a coat, a person or two inside)
The pavement no longer outshines the room and does not read as a tiled CG texture
A closer, more intentional camera: the pair fills about 40% of the frame height, a sliver of sill and pavement, believable glass reflections
Atmosphere: soft pools from the spots on the floor and shelves with visible falloff, faint haze

defects.what: Hard-edged blue-tinted rectangle over the room (b_median 18 vs r_median 8, edge 5 px wide at y~319); reads as a stray glass reflection or a compositing error
Pavement is the brightest area in the frame (lum_median 172) and its tile grid is perfectly regular and clean, an obvious CG texture
Back of the room and ceiling nearly crushed (lum_median 4.3, crush 46.8%, about 16% of the frame); the felt, bar and listening room are lost
Right-wall shelving reads as black slabs (lum_median 8.7, crush 31%); the vertical steel fins have no sheen or edge highlight
Left shelving: the top three shelves are empty except for small white cubes; the record runs are uniform and repeated
The Ember pair reads as glowing red signage with uniform emission; the speaker region's lum_median of 19 is too low for the hero
The teal Tropos and the cyan, purple and green Hemispheres/coins compete with the Ember pair for colour
Sill/plinth band is a flat crushed black strip (crush 19%) with no material or edge
Ceiling and fascia flat dark, with no texture or light
No people, glasses, coats or any sign of life; the shop reads as a closed showroom

changes.problem: The hero pair is underlit and reads as a flat red glow, not lit cast acrylic.

evidence.measured: left cabinet lum_median 29.3, right 34.0; whole pair region [440,375,740,620] lum_median 19.2, crush 13%

change.setting: track spots: the window pair (2 x spot)
change.to: 60.0 W, 2700 K, cone 26.0 deg, aimed slightly from above and in front so the horns' top edges and the cabinet faces pick up a highlight

changes.expected: The pair's cabinets light up, the horn edges glow, the batts are legible and a pool of light lands on the plinth

changes.problem: A hard-edged blue rectangle overlays the middle of the room and immediately reads as an artefact.

evidence.measured: b_median 18 vs r_median 8 and g_median 11, while the neighbouring region [300,320,555,465] is r 15 / b 6; horizontal edge 5 px wide at y~319

change.setting: the shopfront glass reflection / outside: the building opposite
change.from: a cool, flat rectangular plane reflected in the glass (or a stray emitter behind it)
change.to: find the reflected plane and remove it, or replace it with a dim, warm, textured facade (2200-2700 K) so the reflection is low-contrast and has soft edges

changes.expected: The interior behind the glass carries the same warm cast as the rest of the room, with no hard rectangle

changes.problem: The back half of the shop is crushed to black, so the room reads as empty and the frame as too dark.

change.setting: soft light: the back felt's wash; the room's fill
change.to: wash 2.0 W/m2 (2600 K), fill 0.12 W/m2 (2900 K); bar spot 16 W -> 28 W

changes.expected: The felt drapes show folds, the bar and the listening room read as pools of warm light, and the frame median rises into range

changes.problem: The camera is too far back: the pair is small, and the pavement and sill take the bottom quarter of the frame.

evidence.measured: pavement plus sill take 160 of 800 rows (20%); pair is about 245 px tall (31% of the frame)

change.to: position [-3.8, 2.6, 1.35], target [2.4, 3.3, 1.2], lens 40 mm, still level; keep only about 6% pavement at the bottom and lose the top fascia band

changes.expected: The pair fills about 40% of the frame height and the shelves frame it on both sides, so it reads as a window picture with intent

changes.problem: The shelves are nearly empty and there is no sign of life, so it reads as a showroom, not a working shop that plays records.

evidence.measured: seen: the top three left shelves hold only small white cubes; there are no glasses, people or coats anywhere in the frame

change.from: a few record runs and price cubes
change.to: records face-out on the upper left shelves (6-8 sleeves, varied but muted), a record out of its sleeve on the table, two glasses and a bottle on the bar, a coat over a chair, and one or two seated figures in the listening room in silhouette

changes.expected: The shop reads as open and lived-in, and the small highlights on glass and vinyl add sparkle

changes.problem: The pavement outshines the room and its clean, regular tiling is the most CG-looking surface in the frame.

evidence.measured: lum_median 172.4, r 208 / g 166 / b 130, against an interior lum_median of about 12

change.setting: soft light: the street lamp outside; outside: the pavement
change.to: 0.04 W/m2, pavement #3A3835 with a wet, worn concrete-slab texture (varied slabs, joint grime), with light spill from the window falling on it

changes.expected: The pavement sits darker than the speakers and is lit mainly by the shop's spill, which leads the eye in

changes.problem: The right-wall shelving and its steel fins read as black slabs with no sheen.

change.setting: the shelves' LED strips; track spots: the right wall's shelves
change.to: LED 5.0; 55 W, cone 40 deg, aimed to graze the fin edges

changes.expected: The steel fins show a soft edge highlight, and the products on the shelves sit in pools of light

changes.problem: The air is dead clear, so the spots make no pools or atmosphere and the light feels synthetic.

evidence.measured: seen: no visible cones or bloom above the pair or the bar; lum_p5 0.0 in the back region

changes.expected: Faint cones above the pair and the bar, a gentle lift of the blacks, and depth between the window and the felt

out_of_scope.request: Make the Ember cabinets read less like uniform red emission (more visible acrylic thickness, polished edge glow, less saturated body)
out_of_scope.why: The speakers' shape, colour and parts are fixed by the card; only the light on them may change

out_of_scope.request: Reduce the competing saturated colours (teal Tropos, cyan/purple/red Hemispheres, coloured EARFcoins)
out_of_scope.why: The card fixes each product in its tint as placed; dimming their glow is the only lever, and doing so works against the shop being lit

out_of_scope.request: Remove or restyle the black shelving fins and the black plinth
out_of_scope.why: The plan (A-401) fixes where the furniture stands and what it is made of
